Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 82, verse 1–5:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder, and when the stars are scattered, and when the seas are burst forth, and when the graves are overturned, a soul will know what it has sent forward and what it has left behind.﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾ means it is split open; ﴿and when its stars are scattered﴾ means they are scattered from it and fall; ﴿and when the seas are burst forth﴾ means some of them burst into others, so that all of them are filled.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in agreement with what we have said, though they differ on some of it.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and when the seas are burst forth﴾: he said, some of them into others.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and when the seas are burst forth﴾: their sweet water will burst into their salt water, and their salt water into their sweet water.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, ﴿and when the seas are burst forth﴾: he said, some of them burst into others, so their water is gone. Al-Kalbi said: they are filled.

* *

And His saying: ﴿and when the graves are overturned﴾

means: and when the graves are stirred up, and those dead within them are brought out alive. It is said: "Ba'thara Fulan hawd Fulan" when one makes its bottom its top. It is said: "ba'thara" and "bahthara" are two dialectal forms.

The interpreters have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and when the graves are overturned﴾: he said, they are searched (buhithat).

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: every soul will know what it has sent forward for that Day of good deeds that benefit it, and what it has left behind of a matter it established and which was acted upon.

The most correct of these opinions in my view is to say: both are well-known readings (qira'at) among the major cities' reading traditions, and both are correct in meaning. Some readers of Basra read ﴿yawmu﴾ with a damma (raf', nominative), in response to the first "day" (yawm). The nominative is more eloquent in the speech of the Arabs. The reason is that "yawm" is annexed to a present or future verb (yafʿalu), and when the Arabs annex "yawm" to a form such as tafʿalu, yafʿalu or afʿalu, they make it nominative, saying: "This is a day when he does such-and-such." When they annex it to a past verb (fiʿl māḍī), they make it accusative. Among this is the saying of the poet:

*"At the time I reproached white hair for youth,
and said, 'Will you not yet become sober, while grey hair is restraining you?'"*

[Note on the text: his words "aghfal" (he became heedless), an intransitive verb that does not take an object. Its meaning is that he entered into heedlessness and forgetfulness. It is an Arabic form, a known usage, even though it is not found in the lexicons. It is like their saying "anjada" (he entered Najd) and similar forms. It is enough to know that it is Arabic that it is the language of al-Shafi'i, who used it more than others did in his Risala and his Umm. Among that is his saying in the Risala (no. 136, p. 42): "And through imitation, whoever among them became heedless became heedless."]

End of the tafsir of the surah "When the sky is cleft asunder" (Al-Infitar).

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿Indeed, the wicked are surely in Hellfire﴾ (14)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the wicked﴾, those who disbelieve in their Lord, ﴿are surely in Hellfire﴾.

* *

And His words: ﴿They will burn therein on the Day of Recompense﴾ (15)

He, may His praise be exalted, says: These wicked ones will burn in Hellfire on the Day of Resurrection, the Day when servants are called to account for their deeds and are repaid for them.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, explanation of meaning) have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿the Day of Recompense﴾: it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which Allah has magnified and warned His servants against.

* *

And His words: ﴿Nor will they be absent from it﴾ (16)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These wicked ones will never leave Hellfire, nor will they be absent from it. Rather, they will abide in it eternally, and likewise the righteous will abide in bliss. This is like His words: ﴿Nor will they ever be removed from it﴾ (Al-Hijr 15:48, Al-Hijr is not cited here; the verse is ﴿وَمَا هُمْ مِنْهَا بِمُخْرَجِينَ﴾, Al-Hijr 15:48).

* *

And His words: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ (17)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And what made you know, O Muhammad, what the Day of Recompense is? That is, what made you aware of what the Day of Recompense is? He means: what is the Day of Reckoning and Repayment? By this saying, He magnifies its matter, may His remembrance be exalted.

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾: a magnification of the Day of Resurrection, the Day on which people are repaid for their deeds.

* *

And His words: ﴿Then, what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ (18)

He says: Then what is it that made you aware, O Muhammad, of the Day of Repayment and Reckoning, magnifying its matter? Then He, may His praise be exalted, explained some of its matter, saying: ﴿The Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul﴾ (19). He says: That day, ﴿the Day when no soul [will possess anything for another soul]﴾, meaning: the Day on which no soul will avail another soul anything, so as to ward off a calamity that has befallen it, nor will it benefit it with any benefit. In the world, a soul would protect another and ward off from it whoever sought to harm it, but that is nullified on that day, because the command belongs to Allah, whom no overpowerer overpowers and no subduer subdues. There the kingdoms will vanish, the authorities will perish, and sovereignty will belong to the Almighty King. This is His words: ﴿And the command on that Day belongs to Allah﴾, meaning: the whole command on that day, that is, the Judgment, belongs to Allah alone, not to any of His creation. No one among His creation will have any command or prohibition with Him on that day.

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said on this.
